summary: Finished the reactory-azure reference-page work left by the terminated run and closed both reviewer findings. The page is 1,005 lines under 06-modules/reactory-azure/README.md, documents the module honestly as a reference example (MIT, example-only, not a supported commercial integration), reconciles the stale commercial registry value with evidence, maps all ten build steps to real files, and ships a 34-check verifier. Reviewer RC-1 (interface declares eight methods, getEmails is implemented but undeclared, TS2353/TS2339) and RC-2 (sendEmail catches the missing Client and returns the Express response export rather than throwing) were already corrected in commit 20a8ebf; this run verified those fixes against source and added a further correction distinguishing getEmails' catch from the missing-client failure (d58c4d6). All azure checks pass 34/34, reactor 11/11, and core 25/26 with the single pre-existing generated-reference drift untouched by this branch.

findings_documented: The module registers zero services: services/index.ts is `export default []`, so services: [...services] is empty; MSGraph in services/graph.ts is a plain object with no FQN/namespace/version/factory and is never imported by the service index.

MSGraph implements nine methods but IMicrosoftGraph declares eight. getEmails (graph.ts:105) — one of only two methods core calls — is an excess property (TS2353) and absent from the exported type (TS2339 at UserEmails.ts:22).

Client and ResponseType are never imported and the Graph client packages are undeclared, so the eight methods that call the factory outside a try throw `ReferenceError: Client is not defined`; getUserDetails, the path core actually calls, is one of them.

sendEmail calls the factory inside its try, catches and logs the same ReferenceError, then returns the module-scope Express `response` import at :225 — a truthy non-result, so a failed send is indistinguishable from success.
getEmails' catch returns the initialised [] for request errors, but its factory call at :107 precedes the try at :109, so today the missing Client escapes before that catch can run.
The module exposes zero GraphQL types/resolvers, zero models/migrations, zero forms/client plugins/translations/routes/middleware, and zero workflow definitions (workflows/index.ts exports []).

storage/index.ts is an empty class whose methods are entirely commented out, targets the pre-v12 SDK, reads only AZURE_STORAGE_KEY at import time, hardcodes the Azurite account devstoreaccount1, and is imported by nothing.
Core bypasses the module contract with two direct source imports (ProfileResolver.ts:6, UserEmails.ts:9), making azure a compile-time dependency of core rather than a runtime contribution.

The registry contradicts the manifest three ways: package.json/AGENT.md say MIT and README says Example Only, while available.json/enabled-reactory.json/installed.json say commercial and available.json carries a shop URL.
Package identity drifts from module identity: @reactory/azure 1.1.0 vs core.ReactoryAzure@1.0.0.
No tests exist in the module.
